inputs.text: Tens of thousands marched in central London alongside trade unions, anti-racism groups and Muslim representative bodies to stand against far-right politics and its harm to vulnerable communities. Calling that collective action an attempt to silence voters is a way to discredit anti-racist organising without showing that anyone’s debate has actually been shut down. People should be able to discuss social and economic concerns, but that cannot mean giving prejudice a free pass or demanding that targeted communities tolerate it in the name of tradition. We should confront the inequality and insecurity that fuel division—not blame people organising against racism.
